title: The Crab and His Mother
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: An Old Crab said to her son, "Why do you walk sideways like that, my son? You ought to walk straight." The Young Crab replied, "Show me how, dear mother, and I'll follow your example." The Old Crab tried, but tried in vain, and then saw how foolish she had been to find fault with her child.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Old Crab criticize her son for?
options: Eating too slowly
Wandering too far from home
Walking sideways
Hiding under rocks all day

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Old Crab tell her son he ought to do?
options: Walk straight
Walk more slowly
Walk only at night
Walk alongside her at all times

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Young Crab ask his mother to do?
options: Explain why walking straight matters
Ask another crab to teach him instead
Wait until he is older to learn
Show him how to walk straight so he can follow her example

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens when the Old Crab tries to walk straight herself?
options: She succeeds easily on her first attempt
She tries, but tries in vain
She refuses to try at all
She asks the Young Crab to try first instead

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Old Crab realize after her failed attempt?
options: That her son was actually walking correctly all along
That crabs cannot be taught to walk differently
That she had been foolish to find fault with her child
That she needed more practice before trying again

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Young Crab's request expose a problem with his mother's criticism?
options: It reveals that she is asking him to do something she herself cannot do
It shows that he does not actually want to learn to walk straight
It proves that he already knows how to walk straight
It suggests that walking straight is not actually possible for crabs

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Old Crab's realization suggest about giving advice to others?
options: Advice should never be given to one's own children
Advice about walking is different from advice about other habits
Advice is only useful if it comes from someone older
Advice carries less weight when the one giving it cannot follow it themselves

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Old Crab tried "in vain"?
options: Without being noticed
Without success
Without much effort
Without any pain

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean to "find fault with" someone, as the Old Crab did with her child?
options: To praise them warmly for something
To ask them a simple question
To criticize or point out flaws in them
To ignore them entirely

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Setting an example works better than merely telling others what to do
Children should never question their parents' advice
Crabs are physically unable to walk in a straight line
Mothers should avoid criticizing their children at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who speaks first in the conversation?
options: The Young Crab
Neither; they speak at the same time
A third crab observing them
The Old Crab

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Young Crab call his mother when he answers her?
options: "Old Crab"
"Dear mother"
"Teacher"
"Wise one"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Young Crab promise to do if shown how to walk straight?
options: Teach the other young crabs too
Practice every day until he succeeds
Follow his mother's example
Never walk sideways again regardless

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Young Crab ask to be shown rather than simply agreeing to try?
options: He wants his mother to demonstrate the very thing she is asking of him
He does not believe walking straight is possible at all
He is stalling so he does not have to obey her
He wants to compare her walk to his own first

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Old Crab's failed attempt reveal about crabs in general?
options: Only young crabs are able to walk sideways
The Old Crab was simply out of practice
Walking straight is easy but rarely attempted
Walking sideways may simply be how crabs are built to move

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "precept" mean in the closing line "Example is better than precept"?
options: A reward given for good behavior
A rule or instruction telling someone what to do
A story told to entertain children
A tool used for measuring distance

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A son teaches his mother a new way of walking
A mother and son agree that walking sideways is best
A mother's criticism of her son backfires when she cannot do what she demands of him
A mother punishes her son for walking incorrectly
